name: Amendments by the committee responsible – put to the vote collectively
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing the exchange, assistance and training programme for the protection of the euro against counterfeiting for the period 2028-2034 (the 'Pericles V' programme) and repealing Regulation (EU) 2021/840

part_text: (1a) Sound protection of the euro against counterfeiting is a key component of a secure and competitive Union economy and is directly linked to the Union objective of improving the efficient functioning of the economic and monetary union. / (1b) Actions with the aim of promoting exchanges of information and staff, technical and scientific assistance and specialised training help significantly to protect the Union’s single currency against counterfeiting and related fraud, and therefore to attain a high and equivalent level of protection across the Union, whilst demonstrating the Union’s ability to tackle serious organised crime. Such actions could also help address the common challenges in combatting organised crime, including money laundering. / (4a) Independent evaluations of the Pericles IV programme show that it plays a key role in preventing and combatting euro counterfeiting, helping to protect the integrity of euro banknotes and coins. The programme strengthens information exchange, technical expertise, institutional cooperation, and operational capacity, while supporting networking and joint investigations that have led to seizures of counterfeit euros and the disruption of criminal networks. The programme is efficient in its use of resources and complements the work of other Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies including the European Central Bank (ECB), Europol and Eurojust. To remain effective, the programme should continue to adapt to emerging threats such as digital currencies, more sophisticated counterfeits, altered-design banknotes, and the growing online availability of counterfeit materials. / (5) The protection of the European single currency as a public good has a clear transnational dimension, and therefore euro protection goes beyond the interest and the responsibility of individual Member States. Euro cash, which is currently the only means of payment universally accessible to all citizens, promotes financial inclusion by enabling payments irrespective of access to digital technologies or banking services, and serves as a critical instrument of resilience when electronic payment systems are disrupted. The effective performance of its function as legal tender status is dependent upon on the integrity of the single currency itself. Counterfeiting undermines that integrity, imposing uncompensated losses on citizens and businesses and eroding trust in the single currency. Considering the cross-border circulation of the euro and the deep involvement of international organised crime in euro counterfeiting, national protection frameworks should be complemented by Union initiative to ensure homogeneous national and international cooperation, and to face possible emerging transnational risks. Therefore by establishing the exchange, assistance and training programme for the protection of the euro against counterfeiting, this Regulation is necessary, suitable and appropriate for achieving the objectives of the Programme. The Programme should efficiently strengthen cooperation among the Member States and between the Commission and the Member States, without restricting Member States’ capability to protect the euro against counterfeiting. The effectiveness of the Programme depends on flexible, operational and timely cooperation between competent authorities and relevant Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, including through the regular exchange of information on emerging threats, priorities and best practices. The Commission should therefore carry out all necessary consultations with regard to evaluating the needs for the protection of the euro with the principal parties involved, in particular the competent national authorities designated by Member States, the ECB, Europol and Eurojust within the advisory committee referred to in Regulation (EC) No 1338/2001, particularly as regards exchanges, assistance and training, for the purpose of the application of the Programme.
